paper.title_en: Analysis of quasielastic scattering and one-neutron transfer channel in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction
paper.abstract_en: The strong interplay between the nuclear structure and reaction dynamics near the Coulomb barrier makes the reaction observables a powerful tool for probing the structural properties. To disentangle the roles of nuclear deformation and positive <math><mi>Q</mi></math>-value neutron transfer channels, the angular distributions for quasielastic scattering and neutron transfer have been measured for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system and analyzed in the context of the midshell heavy nuclei <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>176</mn></mrow></math>, where inelastic and transfer couplings compete each other. The measured angular distributions for quasielastic and one-neutron transfer have been interpreted in light of coupled reaction calculations using the <math><mi mathvariant="normal" mathsize="small">FRESCO</mi></math> code. Analysis of the quasielastic angular distribution indicated a strong influence of inelastic excitations arising from the large nuclear deformation of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The influence of <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>-pickup channel was calculated in the single-step and sequential modes. The analysis suggests that the <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>-pickup channel have a feeble impact on the angular distribution and the transfer of <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> in step mode more adequately explains the experimental data. Furthermore, the analysis of the angular distribution for one neutron pickup channel suggested a significant contribution from higher energy states compared to lower energy states, which might be due to the large deformation of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The present study validates the reported values of deformation parameters and spectroscopic factors, respectively, for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The results show a significant impact of the collective nature on the spectroscopic behavior of the reaction partners <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, which is reflected in the experimental observables. These measurements provide important input for separating the contributions of positive <math><mi>Q</mi></math>-value transfer channels and nuclear deformation in governing the fusion dynamics.
